children: Singapore's central bank could raise the slope of its monetary policy band "very slightly" in October, says Barclays's Brian Tan in a note. This implies a 25 basis-point adjustment to an estimated 1.50%, the economist says. He views such a move as justified due to likely relatively robust gross domestic product growth into 2027, citing "the sheer magnitude of the artificial-intelligence boom." He raises his 2026 economic growth projection to 5.5% from 4.5% to factor in Singapore's still-firm August nonoil domestic export figures. The Monetary Authority of Singapore uses the exchange rate as a policy tool for maintaining price stability, given the city-state's small and open economy. (megan.cheah@wsj.com)
